outcome: Documentation and profile of maternal and perinatal complications
Improved estimation of maternal and perinatal complications
cohort: The study included 3380 mothers who delivered 3386 newborns (including 6 twins) in eleven government hospitals in Bikaner, India, over a six-month period in 2014.
finding: The Intrapartum Complications Registry documented 828 cases (22.5%) of maternal and perinatal complications, with haemorrhage, prolonged/obstructed labour, and hypertensive disorders being the commonest maternal complications, and low birth weight, birth asphyxia, and neonatal sepsis being the commonest perinatal complications.
cross-section timing: Data was analyzed for a six-month period in 2014.
